subsystems.name: Telescope and spectrograph
subsystems.role: collects the star's light during transit and spreads it into a spectrum fine enough to resolve narrow gas lines.
parts: high-resolution ground spectrograph with stable wavelength calibration

subsystems.name: Transit timing and observing schedule
subsystems.role: ensures the telescope is looking during the few hours the planet crosses the star.
parts: start and end timings including the planet's leading and trailing tails
out-of-transit baseline windows before and after

subsystems.name: Stellar reference and contamination control
subsystems.role: subtracts the star's own absorption and variability, which can mimic or hide a planetary signal.
parts: model of the stellar wind and its interaction with the planet

subsystems.name: Data reduction and calibration pipeline
subsystems.role: turns raw detector counts into a clean, wavelength-calibrated transmission spectrum.
parts: telluric absorption correction (the Earth's atmosphere absorbs at the helium line)

subsystems.name: Escape modelling and retrieval
subsystems.role: converts the measured absorption into a mass-loss rate, outflow speed and temperature.

subsystems.name: High-energy irradiance monitoring
subsystems.role: measures the stellar X-ray and ultraviolet output that drives the escape.

buildSteps.title: Pick a target likely to be escaping
buildSteps.detail: Favour hot, low-density planets on short orbits, where the upper atmosphere is puffed up and the transit chord through the escaping gas is long.

buildSteps.title: Pin down the ephemeris and secure telescope time
buildSteps.detail: Refine the transit timing from survey photometry, then win time on a spectrograph with the right wavelength coverage and resolution.

buildSteps.title: Observe in transit and out of transit
buildSteps.detail: Take many short exposures through the transit plus a baseline before and after, so the star's own spectrum can be divided out.

buildSteps.title: Clean the Earth's atmosphere out of the data
buildSteps.detail: Ground-based observations must remove the telluric helium absorption, which sits at almost the same wavelength and varies with airmass.

buildSteps.title: Model and subtract stellar activity
buildSteps.detail: Fit the star's lines and variability using activity indicators and contemporaneous photometry, leaving the residual planetary signal.

buildSteps.title: Extract the line absorption
buildSteps.detail: Compare in-transit and out-of-transit spectra in the line core; a deeper absorption during transit means gas is present outside the planet's solid body.

buildSteps.title: Convert the signal into a mass-loss rate
buildSteps.detail: Fit escape models to the line profile and depth to estimate how much gas leaves per second, and at what speed.

buildSteps.title: Add the energy budget and interpret
buildSteps.detail: Combine the mass-loss estimate with the star's X-ray and ultraviolet output to judge whether the planet is losing its atmosphere quickly enough to strip it over its lifetime.

prerequisites.tech: Space telescopes with ultraviolet and near-infrared spectroscopy
prerequisites.why: only above the atmosphere can hydrogen Lyman-alpha and much of the near-infrared be observed at all.

prerequisites.tech: High-resolution ground spectrographs with stable calibration
prerequisites.why: the helium line at 1083 nanometres is a narrow feature that needs fine spectral resolution and precise wavelength stability.

prerequisites.tech: Precise transit ephemerides from photometric surveys
prerequisites.why: the observing window is only hours long, so the predicted transit time must be accurate.
escape is driven by high-energy starlight, but the extreme-ultraviolet part must largely be reconstructed rather than measured directly.

prerequisites.tech: Telluric and stellar contamination models at high precision
prerequisites.why: the residual planetary signal is a fraction of a percent, comparable to the systematic errors that remain in the data.

pathway.milestone: helium escape detected around dozens of transiting planets, from hot gas giants to Neptune-sized worlds, using space and ground spectrographs
pathway.unlocks: a working tracer of atmospheric loss that can be applied to many systems.

pathway.milestone: broad surveys combining escape measurements with stellar age and activity and with planetary mass and radius
pathway.unlocks: evidence on whether escape sculpts the observed gap between rocky and Neptune-sized planets.

pathway.milestone: escape measured for small planets around cool, low-mass stars, whose high-energy output is intense and long-lived
pathway.unlocks: a clearer picture of whether such planets can hold onto atmospheres at all.

pathway.milestone: a large future ultraviolet-optical-infrared space telescope, such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory concept, able to resolve weak metal lines routinely
pathway.unlocks: escape budgets for faint, small and long-period planets, not just the brightest hot ones.
